number.why: JSON numbers compare by value; 1e-9 absorbs only float formatting/rounding of the same arithmetic (EMU/12700 point conversions), never a different layout.

raster.why: Rendered pixels (PDF figure clips, Chromium page previews) must have identical dimensions; per-channel mean |difference| over RGBA <= 2/255 and at most 1% of pixels whose largest RGB channel difference exceeds 48 absorb anti-aliasing, resampling and codec differences, while a moved, missing or recoloured element fails.

ooxml.why: A package compares as its part set; .xml/.rels parts by C14N 2.0 canonical form (attribute order, namespace prefixes declaration placement and inter-element whitespace are not semantic) with the creation/modification timestamps masked; ZIP entry order, timestamps and compression are ignored; nested .xlsx/.docx/.pptx parts recurse; .fntdata parts compare as fonts; every other part byte-exact.

font.why: An embedded font part compares by family/subfamily name and its exact cmap codepoint set (the glyph coverage the subset promises), not by bytes: subsetters legitimately differ in table layout and glyph order.

bytes.why: Imported media and other opaque blobs are byte-exact (sha256).

text.why: Strings, including extracted text, Markdown and HTML, are exact after the per-operation normalizations below. No whitespace or Unicode normalization is tolerated.

pdf.parse.why: sizeKB is the encoded size of the figure clip, which depends on the PNG/JPEG encoder; the pixels are compared with the raster rule.

slides.import_html.why: @font-face rules keep family, weight and format; the file:// URL of the host font cache becomes {font-file}.

slides.pptx_preview.why: Link boxes are page fractions measured from browser layout; 0.002 of the page is under 3 px at 1280 px.

slides.inspect_pptx.why: Package byte size depends on ZIP compression.

slides.export_pptx.why: Byte sizes depend on ZIP compression and the font subsetter; the package itself is compared with the ooxml rule.
